title: The Silver Bullet for Lesson Planning: Atomisation with AI
author: Dario Emanuele
summary: Dario Emanuele describes a first experiment using Google's Gemini 3.0 model to help plan lessons by 'atomising' curriculum content -- breaking it into the small, tightly-sequenced steps that Rosenshine's Principles of Instruction call for -- and reports that the AI-assisted process produced a usable, well-structured plan far faster than doing it manually. Emanuele frames this as a genuine advance over earlier AI planning attempts because the newer model's reasoning is strong enough to handle the decomposition step itself, rather than just generating generic worksheets or slides. He is explicit that this is an early, imperfect experiment rather than a finished method, and closes the piece by asking readers to actually try his shared resources and prompts, and to report back on how well the process worked in their own subjects and schools. The tone is exploratory and collaborative rather than promotional -- Emanuele positions himself as testing a workflow in public rather than announcing a solved problem.
points: Emanuele's key claim is that Gemini 3.0's improved reasoning makes it capable of doing the atomisation step itself -- decomposing a topic into Rosenshine-aligned small steps -- rather than just producing generic AI-generated worksheets or slides.

He frames the post explicitly as a 'first experiment,' not a finished method, and asks readers directly for feedback on quality, access issues, and results in their own classrooms -- treating this as public workflow-testing rather than a polished announcement.

The piece continues Emanuele's established pattern (seen across his 'Atomisation and HTML' series) of using AI to solve the labour-intensive parts of lesson planning while keeping the underlying pedagogical principle (atomisation, per Rosenshine) fixed.

By sharing his actual prompts and resource files rather than describing them abstractly, Emanuele invites direct replication -- a build-guide structure aimed specifically at working teachers rather than a general AI/tech audience.
quotes: I am excited to see how this ‘first experiment’ works across different schools and subjects, and I need your help to make the definitive version even better.
Feedback is Gold: Please, please, please send me any and all feedback: messages, emails, anything! Did it work awfully? Did you have issues accessing the files? What was the quality of the plan?
Share the Power: If you find this useful, share the gem with colleagues, both in and outside your school, across any subject.

In the past, I would have used perhaps 20-30% of the teaching ideas and atoms the Gem suggested. Now, the planning is so precise, I am regularly using most of the atoms and teaching ideas it produces.

Human Expertise is Key: Not every lesson plan the Gem produces is perfect. Your expert judgment, your knowledge of your class, the common misconceptions, and the specific curriculum nuance, is essential. The Gem provides a robust super-scaffold for planning, but the teacher remains the architect.
